1.why: The UI uses a clean sans-serif typeface with comfortable letter and line spacing on every screen.

2.why: No italics, all-caps text, or dense paragraphs appear; labels and instructions are short sentence case.

3.why: Single-column card layout with large inputs and buttons is clearly arranged for a mobile viewport.

4.why: Copy such as “Set up an extra check for protected payments” and step titles is short and plain.

5.why: Email, mobile, identity-code and authenticator-code fields show no placeholders or format examples.

6.why: Every step contains only brief labels or a short list; no long prose must be read to continue.

7.why: Manual secret and recovery codes are rendered as ordinary selectable text that can be copied, though no copy button is present.

8.why: Authenticator setup shows only a manual secret string; no QR code or equivalent alternative is offered.

9.why: Standard email and telephone inputs are used (typically autofill-friendly), but no explicit password-manager or autocomplete support is visible.

10.why: Clear step headings (e.g. “Verify your identity”) and high-contrast blue primary buttons make the current step and action obvious.

11.why: Most screens present a single primary button; the authenticator step still keeps one main confirm action after code creation.

12.why: Screens advance with new titles and the final page states “Multi-factor authentication is active,” but intermediate steps lack explicit “what happened / next” feedback.

13.why: Error banner allows retry and generate buttons remain, yet no reveal/hide or re-request controls for codes are shown.

14.why: The message “We could not complete that request. Please try again.” avoids blame but does not name the problem or a concrete fix.

15.why: No countdown timers, expiry notices or time limits appear on any of the ten screens.
